content: Meropenem is a carbapenem-type antibiotic used to treat a wide range of bacterial infections. It is typically prescribed when your doctor determines that the benefits outweigh the potential risks. This medication may cause side effects such as swelling, redness, pain, or soreness at the injection site, as well as upset stomach, headache, nausea, vomiting, constipation, or diarrhea. Rarely, it can lead to more severe conditions, such as a serious intestinal infection caused by Clostridium difficile, which may occur during or even weeks to months after treatment has ended. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may result in oral thrush or a new yeast infection. Before using meropenem, inform your doctor if you are allergic to it, other carbapenems (e.g., imipenem), penicillins, cephalosporins, or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other issues. Rarely, meropenem may cause headaches, numbness or tingling of the skin, or seizures. Some forms of this medication contain sodium, which may be relevant for patients on sodium-restricted diets. Additionally, meropenem may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. This medication can also pass into breast milk, so consult your doctor if you are breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. It is essential to maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs, as well as herbal products, and share this information with your doctor and pharmacist. If someone overdoses and experiences severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. If you miss a dose, consult your doctor or pharmacist promptly for a new dosing schedule. Proper storage of the medication is important; follow the product instructions and consult your pharmacist for details. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Discard expired or unused medication properly. While using this medication, your doctor may recommend laboratory or medical tests, such as a complete blood count or kidney function tests, to monitor your progress and check for side effects. Keep all medical and laboratory appointments as scheduled. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
